Run the Historical Period and Summarise Present-Day Immunity

Source: R/immunity_history.R
run_immunity_history.Rd

Runs the model from the first year of data (1950) to the start of `year_end` for one country and disease, under a stated assumption about reporting, and returns the state at the end together with diagnostics that show what the assumption implies.

Usage

run_immunity_history(
  iso,
  disease,
  R0,
  transmission_history = c("circulating_years", "reported_cases_only"),
  circulation_threshold = 2,
  reporting_fraction = 1,
  coverage_accuracy = 1,
  vaccine_waning = "default",
  coverage_source = c("wuenic", "median"),
  seed_floor = 10,
  year_end = "",
  seed = 1,
  keep_params = FALSE,
  snapshot_years = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

iso

A 3-letter ISO country code.

disease

`"measles"`, `"diphtheria"` or `"pertussis"`.

R0

Basic reproduction number while transmission is on.

transmission_history, circulation_threshold, reporting_fraction, coverage_accuracy, vaccine_waning, coverage_source, seed_floor

The historical assumptions; see [data_load_process_wrapper()].

year_end

The state returned is that at the start of this year. Default (`""`) is the current year.

seed

Seed for the model's random number stream. Different seeds give different stochastic histories, which mainly sets where in its epidemic cycle a setting is at the end.

keep_params

Logical; return the parameter list too? Default `FALSE`.

snapshot_years

Years at whose start to record immunity by age (as in `by_age`), for example the years of several serosurveys, so that one run serves them all. Years outside the run are dropped with a warning. Default `NULL`, none.

...

Further arguments passed to [custom_data_process_wrapper()] (for example custom data).

Value

A list of class `prevail_immunity_history` with:

`iso`, `disease`, `R0`, `seed`, `year_start`, `year_end`

What was run. The state is at the start of `year_end`.

`assumptions`

The historical assumptions used.

`summary`

`reff` (the effective reproduction number at `R0`, see [effective_reproduction_number()]), `population`, `susceptible` (effective susceptibility), `vaccinated` and `infected`.

`by_age`

Immunity by age group and source; see [summarise_immunity()].

`infections`

By year: modelled infections (all ages and under five), reported cases, the reporting fraction this implies (reported cases over modelled infections), seeded infections and whether transmission was on.

`infections_by_age`

Modelled infections by year (rows, named by year) and age group (columns).

`snapshots`

Immunity by age at the start of each of `snapshot_years`: the columns of `by_age` with a `year` column first, or `NULL` if none were asked for.

`coverage`

By age group and dose: the share of the age group that has had at least that many doses at the end of the run (`achieved`) against the mean reported routine coverage in the years its birth cohorts were due the dose (`reported`). Campaign doses, the coverage accuracy and, where vaccine protection wanes, waning out of a stratum all move `achieved` away from `reported`.

`state`

`S0`, `I0` (exposed and infectious) and `Rpop0` (recovered) by age group, vaccination stratum and risk group, rounded to whole people, ready to start a projection from; and `compartments`, the six model compartments unrounded.

`inputs`

Routine coverage and age group by dose in the final year, the final year's vaccination rates, protection and waning by stratum, whether the disease is taken to be circulating now, and the age distribution of the population.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
h <- run_immunity_history("GBR", "measles", R0 = 15, year_end = 2025)
h$summary$reff
h$by_age
} # }
